Bundle of nine (9) test patients and associated data that exhaustively illustrate population criteria semantics across the four scoring types: proportion, ratio, continuous-variable, and cohort.
Cohort test case — Ada has an Encounter, so is counted in the cohort; other resources are present but not evaluated (cohort has no exclusions).
Cohort test case — Ben has an Encounter, so is counted in the cohort; other resources are present but not evaluated (cohort has no exclusions).
Cohort test case — Cyd has no Encounter, so is not in the cohort.
Cohort test case — Dev has an Encounter, so is counted in the cohort; other resources are present but not evaluated (cohort has no exclusions).
Cohort test case — Eve has an Encounter, so is counted in the cohort; other resources are present but not evaluated (cohort has no exclusions).
Cohort test case — Fin has an Encounter, so is counted in the cohort; other resources are present but not evaluated (cohort has no exclusions).
Cohort test case — Gus has an Encounter, so is counted in the cohort; other resources are present but not evaluated (cohort has no exclusions).
Cohort test case — Hana has no Encounter, so is not in the cohort.
Cohort test case — Ivy has an Encounter, so is counted in the cohort; other resources are present but not evaluated (cohort has no exclusions).
Summary test case for cohort measure IGCohort over the nine shared example patients. Expected initial-population 7; the cohort score is that member count.
Continuous-variable test case — Ada is a measure-population member; its observation value 2 feeds the aggregate.
Continuous-variable test case — Ben is a measure-population member; its observation value 0 feeds the aggregate.
Continuous-variable test case — Cyd is not in the initial population (no Encounter); its observation value 9 is not counted.
Continuous-variable test case — Dev is measure-population-excluded (deceased); its observation value 4 is not counted.
Continuous-variable test case — Eve is a measure-population member; its observation value 1 feeds the aggregate.
Continuous-variable test case — Fin is a measure-population member; its observation value 0 feeds the aggregate.
Continuous-variable test case — Gus is a measure-population member; its observation value 3 feeds the aggregate.
Continuous-variable test case — Hana is not in the initial population (no Encounter); its observation value 0 is not counted.
Continuous-variable test case — Ivy is in the initial population only (no Procedure); its observation value 7 is not counted.

Summary test case for continuous-variable measure IGContinuousVariable over the nine shared example patients. Expected initial-population 7, measure-population 6, measure-population-exclusion 1, measure-observation 5; observations [0, 0, 1, 2, 3] aggregated by median = 1.
Proportion test case — Ada is in the Denominator and meets the Numerator (a proportion pass).
Proportion test case — Ben is in the Denominator but does not meet the Numerator.
Proportion test case — Cyd is not in the initial population (no Encounter), so the Denominator and Numerator criteria evaluate true but are gated out.
Proportion test case — Dev is Denominator-excluded (deceased), so the Numerator is gated out even though its criterion evaluates true.
Proportion test case — Eve is meets the Numerator but is then Numerator-excluded.
Proportion test case — Fin is a Denominator exception — no Numerator, with a qualifying Condition.
Proportion test case — Gus is in the Denominator and meets the Numerator (a proportion pass).
Proportion test case — Hana is not in the initial population (no Encounter), so the Denominator and Numerator criteria evaluate true but are gated out.
Proportion test case — Ivy is in the initial population but not the Denominator (no Procedure).

Summary test case for proportion measure IGProportion over the nine shared example patients. Expected initial-population 7, denominator 6, denominator-exclusion 1, numerator 3, numerator-exclusion 1, denominator-exception 1; measure score 0.5 = (3 − 1) / (6 − 1 − 1).
Ratio test case — Ada: denominator branch = in the denominator; numerator branch = in the numerator.
Ratio test case — Ben: denominator branch = in the denominator; numerator branch = not in the initial population.

Ratio test case — Cyd: denominator branch = not in the initial population; numerator branch = in the numerator — counts in the numerator with no denominator, which a proportion measure cannot represent.
Ratio test case — Dev: denominator branch = denominator-excluded; numerator branch = in the numerator — stays in the numerator despite denominator exclusion, since the branches are independent.
Ratio test case — Eve: denominator branch = in the denominator; numerator branch = numerator-excluded.
Ratio test case — Fin: denominator branch = in the denominator; numerator branch = not in the initial population.
Ratio test case — Gus: denominator branch = in the denominator; numerator branch = in the numerator.
Ratio test case — Hana: denominator branch = not in the initial population; numerator branch = not in the initial population.
Ratio test case — Ivy: denominator branch = in the initial population only; numerator branch = not in the initial population.

Summary test case for ratio measure IGRatio over the nine shared example patients. Expected initial-population 1 (denominator branch) 7, initial-population 2 (numerator branch) 5, denominator 6, denominator-exclusion 1, numerator 5, numerator-exclusion 1; ratio 0.8 = (5 − 1) / (6 − 1), counted independently.

Bundle of eight (8) test patients and associated data for the Diabetes Care Weighted Composite and its HbA1c poor control (proportion), emergency department visit rate (ratio), and days to follow-up after discharge (continuous variable) components.

Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Poor Control (> 9%) test case. Alma (50) has diabetes and an office visit. Her most recent HbA1c (7.2%) is controlled, although an earlier result (9.8%) was not. She has no emergency department visits and no inpatient stays.

Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Poor Control (> 9%) test case. Boris (62) has diabetes. His most recent HbA1c (10.1%) indicates poor control, although an earlier result (7.5%) was controlled. He has two emergency department visits, and an inpatient discharge on March 10 followed by an office visit 7 days later.

Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Poor Control (> 9%) test case. Cleo (45) has diabetes but no HbA1c test during the measurement period, so she meets the numerator of the (inverse) HbA1c poor control measure. She has one emergency department visit, and an inpatient discharge on June 1 followed by an office visit 11 days later.

Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Poor Control (> 9%) test case. Dmitri (70) has diabetes and a controlled HbA1c (8.1%). He has no emergency department visits. He has an inpatient discharge on September 5, but his first office visit afterwards is 45 days later, so the discharge is in the initial population but not the measure population of the follow-up measure.

Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Poor Control (> 9%) test case. Esme (58) has diabetes and receives hospice care during the measurement period, so she meets the denominator exclusion of the HbA1c and emergency department visit measures, and her discharge (followed by an office visit 5 days later) meets the measure population exclusion of the follow-up measure.

Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Poor Control (> 9%) test case. Felix (80) has diabetes, a poorly controlled HbA1c (11.0%), an emergency department visit, and a discharge with timely follow-up, but is older than 75 and so is not in the initial population of any component.

Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Poor Control (> 9%) test case. Greta (40) has an elevated HbA1c (10.0%), an emergency department visit, and a discharge with timely follow-up, but does not have a diagnosis of diabetes and so is not in the initial population of any component.

Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Poor Control (> 9%) test case. Hugo (33) has diabetes and a controlled HbA1c (6.5%), and no emergency department visits. He has two inpatient discharges, followed by office visits 3 and 12 days later, so he contributes two observations to the follow-up measure.

name.value: MeasureReport Diabetes Care Weighted Composite Summary

description.value: Summary test case for the Diabetes Care Weighted Composite, calculated from the component summary test cases. Component scores 0.4 (HbA1c poor control), 50 per 1,000 patient-months (ED visits), and 9 days (median days to follow-up) normalize to 0.4, 0.5, and 0.3, adjust (decrease) to 0.6, 0.5, and 0.7, and with weights 0.4, 0.3, and 0.3 give an expected composite score of 0.6.

description.value: Bundle of thirteen (13) test patients and associated data for the Preventive Care and Wellness composite measures and their breast cancer screening, colorectal cancer screening, high blood pressure screening, pneumococcal vaccination, and tobacco use screening and cessation components.

Breast Cancer Screening test case. Iris (60) receives every preventive service she is eligible for: a mammogram, a colonoscopy, normal blood pressure at both visits, and tobacco screening (never smoked). She is not old enough for pneumococcal vaccination.

Breast Cancer Screening test case. Jack (68) has a fecal occult blood test and pneumococcal vaccination, and is a tobacco user who receives cessation counseling, but his prehypertensive blood pressure readings have no documented follow-up at either visit.
Breast Cancer Screening test case. Kate (55) has a FIT-DNA test within 3 years and normal blood pressure, but no mammogram, and is a tobacco user who does not receive cessation intervention.

Breast Cancer Screening test case. Liam (45) has two visits: a normal blood pressure at the first, and a prehypertensive reading without follow-up at the second, so one of his two encounters meets the blood pressure screening numerator. He is not screened for tobacco use.

Breast Cancer Screening test case. Mona (70) receives hospice care, so she meets the denominator exclusion of the breast cancer, colorectal cancer, and pneumococcal vaccination components (even though she has the services). Blood pressure and tobacco screening have no hospice exclusion, and she meets both.

Breast Cancer Screening test case. Nate (72) has an existing diagnosis of hypertension, which excludes his encounters from the blood pressure screening component, and colon cancer, which excludes him from colorectal cancer screening. He has not received pneumococcal vaccination. These ongoing conditions are not limited life expectancy conditions, so they do not make him a tobacco screening denominator exception.

Breast Cancer Screening test case. Olga (66) has a mammogram within 27 months and pneumococcal vaccination, but her most recent colonoscopy is more than 10 years old. Her blood pressure was not obtained for a medical reason at her first visit (a denominator exception) but was normal at her preventive visit. She has a limited life expectancy, which is a denominator exception for tobacco screening.

Breast Cancer Screening test case. Paul (30) has a single preventive visit, with a first hypertensive blood pressure reading and no documented follow-up. He is a tobacco user who receives cessation counseling.

Breast Cancer Screening test case. Quinn (52) receives every preventive service she is eligible for: a mammogram, a flexible sigmoidoscopy within 5 years, normal blood pressure at both visits, and tobacco screening (never smoked).

Breast Cancer Screening test case. Rosa (80) is too old for breast and colorectal cancer screening, and has only one office visit, so she is not in the tobacco screening initial population. She has pneumococcal vaccination and a normal blood pressure.
Breast Cancer Screening test case. Sam (17) is younger than 18 at the start of the measurement period, so he is not in the initial population of any component.
